races.name: Hadwins Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Newbrook Diamond
runners_data.note: Course-fit and stamina are the key angles — five-year runner-up on Good ground and a recent Goodwood winner on Good, Gordon Elliott yard in strong form (T14: 10/59), and a prominent style that should see him slot in directly behind Nightflyer at Cartmel's tight turns; 15 days since last run is ideal freshness.|

runners_data.name: Rebel Tribesman
runners_data.note: Strong recent record on Good ground (4/4 similar-going, 2 wins) and Gavin Sheehan a competent partner, but his natural prominent style is squeezed out by the field's make-up and he is unlikely to secure that position naturally — treat his chance as conditional on an unusually fluid early move|

runners_data.name: Viscountess Nelson
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's runner has won and placed twice on Good ground and steps up to a trip that should suit given stamina in pedigree; Mr Daniel Williams claims 7lb which helps the handicap burden, though the amateur jockey element introduces execution risk at a specialist track like Cartmel|

runners_data.name: Nightflyer
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-maker whose controlled front-running could be his undoing or his salvation — four-year-old with no Good-ground wins in recent form (0W0P from 2 outings), and at 2m6f he stretches beyond his previous 2m distance range, making the STYLE_FIT flag relevant as his stamina reserves will be tested if he sets the tempo alone|

runners_data.name: Frisky Whiskey
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type forced wide of his natural hunting ground by the race's shape — three recent efforts on Good have all been finishing positions of 4th-6th, suggesting he finds one too good rather than finishing strongly, and the tongue tie adds a query; 27 days fresh is fine but profile is low-ceiling here|

runners_data.name: Order Another One
runners_data.note: Only one run in the dataset (7th on Good, 17f) gives very little to work with; Ryan Mania is a capable claimer partner and Dianne Sayer's yard placed 0/1 in the 14-day window — a hold-up horse with scant evidence of the stamina this 2m6f trip at Cartmel demands|

runners_data.name: Manhatane
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's four-year-old carries the lowest weight (142lbs) and is ridden by Leah Noreci taking 7lb, but a single form run (5th, 22f, Good) and a P (pulled up) in recent outings makes this the most uncertain profile in the race; the hold-up style needs a strong pace to aim at which this race shape is unlikely to provide|

races.paceDynamic: Nightflyer is the confirmed front runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 2m6f trip on Good ground at Cartmel — a track that demands stamina and jumping accuracy through its tight turns. With no genuine rival willing to press from the front, Nightflyer should control tempo from flag to finish, likely producing a measured early pace that keeps the race together before the final climb. Rebel Tribesman and Frisky Whiskey are both natural prominent and hold-up types respectively who are pushed out of their ideal positions by the field's shape — Newbrook Diamond and Viscountess Nelson are better placed to actually secure the prominent ground directly behind the leader. This race shape — a single front runner dictating a controlled gallop on a stamina track — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel comfortably in the slipstream and produce their effort with energy conserved, rather than closers needing a strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nightflyer Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer leads at a measured clip and prominent-tracking rivals travel smoothly to deliver a late challenge
scenarios.body: Nightflyer sets a manageable pace through Cartmel's turns, leaving prominent horses like Newbrook Diamond and Viscountess Nelson perfectly positioned to pounce at the top of the home straight; Good ground rewards those who jump well and conserve energy in the early stages rather than grinding from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Nightflyer Front-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer's controlled lead is never genuinely threatened and rivals leave their challenge too late
scenarios.body: Nightflyer's uncontested early fractions mean no energy is wasted, and with a small field of seven and no real presser, the leader can bowl along without ever getting into a fight; if the hold-up horses fail to land a blow — as their recent form and style mismatch suggests — the front runner simply goes clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If Nightflyer sets an overly slow pace that bunches the field and turns the race into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: A false-tempo race tightens the contest and can drag back-markers into contention, but this scenario is undermined by the fact that Frisky Whiskey and Order Another One — the true hold-up runners — carry limited form credentials and style-fit concerns at this trip and distance

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Grinds Out Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground rides firmer than expected and errors or fatigue thin the field over the final circuit
scenarios.body: Cartmel's undulations can expose any horse lacking stamina or jumping fluency, and a race of natural attrition over 2m6f could see a well-staying hold-up type emerge if prominent horses flame out; however the thin recent-form profiles of Manhatane and Order Another One make this the least likely winning scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Newbrook Diamond's jumping at the early Cartmel fences — Gordon Elliott's horse has the best profile for this shape but any errors at the tight-turning obstacles in the back straight would undermine his prominent position and hand the initiative to Nightflyer unchallenged.

Watch whether Rebel Tribesman can physically push past Newbrook Diamond and Viscountess Nelson to claim a genuine prominent position at the start — if he cannot, his strong Good-ground record becomes much harder to convert.

Watch Nightflyer's sectionals through the middle mile — if Jonjo O'Neill Jr. allows the pace to drop very low through the back, the race shape flips and hold-up types such as Order Another One gain marginal but unexpected relevance.

Watch Manhatane's jumping early — a four-year-old with a pulled-up run in recent form and a 7lb claimer in the saddle at a course that punishes jumping errors is the runner most likely to exit the race before the home turn.

Watch the Nicky Henderson yard's instructions for Viscountess Nelson — if the stable's runner is produced aggressively to track Nightflyer in second from the outset, she becomes the most direct threat to Newbrook Diamond's preferred berth and alters the first-circuit dynamics for the whole small field.

races.name: Cartmel Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with solid course-distance form, finishing third on good ground twice in the last ten runs; Sean Quinlan's 14-day freshness angle is a minor positive, and his best effort came over a similar 17f trip, suggesting Cartmel's 2m1f suits his stamina profile well.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Despite the name suggesting front-running, this five-year-old is a confirmed hold-up type who has posted three consecutive thirds on good ground, the last two over 16f; Jonathan England gets on well for Sam England's small string, but having raced only three days ago, recovery from a recent outing is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's seven-year-old is fitted with a tongue-tie and hood, having recorded a string of midfield finishes without converting; at OR 94 he is the highest-rated hold-up horse in the field and on pedigree should handle this good ground, but five runs without a win and a STYLE_FIT flag temper confidence that he can assert from a disadvantaged position today.

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Harriet Dickin has landed just zero from three in the last fortnight and this five-year-old arrives on a short three-day turnaround; fitted with a hood and tongue-tie, her form figures on good ground read 3-6-8 in recent outings and the distance looks tight for a horse whose best placing came over 16f on softer ground.

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: George Bewley's seven-year-old is a patient hold-up type who is most comfortable over 20f; the step down to 2m1f at Cartmel is a notable concern, and while he found a placing at 16f recently, his form over shorter trips on good ground is thin — the STYLE_FIT tag underlines that he is unlikely to get his preferred race shape today.

runners_data.name: Alvesta
runners_data.note: The sole winner in this field, Brian Hughes takes over on a five-year-old who scored over 17f on good ground 22 days ago; her winning run came from a hold-up position and the form of that race has solid substance, making her the most interesting among the hold-up contingent if the pace is sufficient to set up a late charge down Cartmel's short home straight.

runners_data.name: Ribble River
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter and race shape architect, Danny McMenamin will press on from the front on OR 76 and has the tactical luxury of an uncontested lead; two wins from 15 similar-ground starts show she can handle these conditions, though the STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges she is technically a prominent rather than a pure lead horse, and whether she has the class to hold off better-rated rivals is the core question.

runners_data.name: Mr Globalist
runners_data.note: Lizzie Quinlan's stablemate of Ribble River, this seven-year-old wears a visor and has been placed four times in good-ground races over 16-17f without winning in 14 career starts; his redistribution into midfield is an accurate reflection of where he will end up racing, and from that unfavoured position on a track that rewards positional play, his prospects of reversing the pattern are limited.

races.paceDynamic: Ribble River is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice handicap and, with no other genuine pace-maker to press her, Danny McMenamin can control fractions from the front and dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop around Cartmel's tight, turning track. The remainder of the field — Mr Lincoln, Made All, Animato, Daring To Dream, King Kodiak, Alvesta and Mr Globalist — are all natural hold-up or wait-and-pounce types, meaning Ribble River will be gifted an uncontested lead and the race is likely to be run at a measured, unhurried pace until the tempo lifts on the final bend. This field is stacked with true hold-up horses, far more than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Ribble River is certain to secure the front, with Mr Lincoln and Made All most likely to press into a prominent berth from their hold-up bases, while the rest are consigned further back than their jockeys would ideally prefer. A steady, front-runner-dominated shape on good ground at Cartmel — a tight, galloping-unfriendly circuit — strongly favours horses that can travel close to a controlled pace and pick up, making prominent trackers and class hold-up horses capable of closing on a flat final stretch the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ribble River Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ribble River bowls along at a fair but sustainable clip and no rival is able or willing to close the gap before the last bend.
scenarios.body: Ribble River dictates every yard, setting a pace that drains her rivals without ever becoming frantic, and McMenamin times the sprint for home to maximise her stamina on this quirky track; horses who need a truly strong pace to get competitive are left with nothing to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ribble River's lead is modest enough that the closest pursuers — Mr Lincoln and Made All — travel within striking distance throughout and produce their effort in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mr Lincoln, who has finished third twice in similar conditions, and Made All, whose consistent form on good ground is a clear asset, would both be ideally positioned to sweep past a tiring front-runner if she has emptied in the last half-mile; this scenario rewards horses that have naturally crept forward from their hold-up roles to sit in a prominent spot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to string the field out and a well-handicapped closer finds a clear run to pick off rivals inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Alvesta, the only horse in the field with a win to her name on good ground over a similar trip, is best placed among the genuine hold-up types to produce a late thrust if her rider Brian Hughes can thread through on the track's short home straight; Animato and King Kodiak are capable of similar moves but carry headgear concerns and have struggled for consistency.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Scrambled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ribble River dawdles to an unusually slow tempo and the race becomes a sprint from two out, creating a bunched, chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: A messy, slow-run race compresses the field, removing the advantage of any single running style and opening the race to those with raw class or a sharp turn of foot; Animato and Daring To Dream, both carrying headgear and capable of quickening if the race falls right, would be among those whose chances lengthen in this scenario, though their recent form makes them speculative.

watchPoints.text: Ribble River's early pace judgement is pivotal — if McMenamin allows her to stride too freely from the outset on this tight Cartmel circuit she could empty before the straight, transforming what looks like a likely winning scenario into a chasing pack opportunity for Mr Lincoln and Alvesta.

Alvesta's recent win came just 22 days ago and Brian Hughes has multiple hold-up horses in the same division; watch how quickly she travels in the early stages, as getting buried behind a slowly-run pack on Cartmel's limited straight would seriously compromise her chance of repeating that form.

Made All returns just three days after a previous run — monitor the paddock for any signs of fatigue or tension, as a horse running for the third time in a short period can often perform below expectations if not visibly fresh.

Animato and King Kodiak are both fitted with hood/tongue-tie combinations and have been repositioned further forward than their true running style warrants; if either manages to slot into a genuinely prominent pitch against expectations, their form profile at this level would make them more dangerous than their recent finishing positions suggest.

Cartmel's track places a premium on jumping fluently around the bends — Mr Globalist's visor and history of midfield finishes in a field of this nature means any jumping errors on the tight turns would cost him ground he cannot recover on the run-in.

races.name: RF Miller & Co Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle Race (Female Professional Jockeys And Amateur Riders' Race)

runners_data.name: My Chiquita
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1-2-2 in last three) over hurdles on Good ground is the standout CV here, and at 7 years old she travels prominently and jumps tidily; 56 days off is no concern given James Moffatt's record freshening horses, and 13 from 15 sim-going runs underlines how well she handles these conditions.
runners_data.comment: My Chiquita won last time out, adding to a placed record of two seconds and a third in her last four starts, and she has run over today's trip and ground before. Top-rated on our figures at 127, with only a 56-day absence to note.

runners_data.name: Saligo Bay
runners_data.note: Arrives 168 days off the track but has won three of eight Good-ground starts and recorded back-to-back wins at 16f on Soft before her last run; Sam England's 1/6 14-day record suggests the yard is in decent form, and she is a natural prominent type who will need the race fitness to be there from the front on a sharp course like Cartmel.
runners_data.comment: Saligo Bay won three in a row before a below-par 5th and unplaced effort, and he has run over today's trip and ground before. A creditable second on our figures, but a 168-day absence since his last outing is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Percy Shelley
runners_data.note: Visored and consistently prominent, with 14 of 15 runs on Good ground making him an ideal surface fit; the 35-day break is fine, and second in a 20f Good handicap last time out shows he stays and battles — James Owen's yard has been firing (8/48 over 14 days) which is a useful context flag.
runners_data.comment: Percy Shelley was runner-up last time out and third two starts back, with a win among his last five outings despite one pulled-up effort. He has run over today's ground before and sits third on our figures - respected.

runners_data.name: Eternal Angel
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the pivot around which this entire race is built; two wins at 16f on Good ground in recent form, handled well fresh (11 days), and Alice Stevens claims 3lb — Tom Lacey's 1/5 14-day record is modest but the horse's own profile is compelling on this track at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Eternal Angel won last time out and again three starts back, and returns just 11 days after that latest win. Two below-par fifths further back temper the case, but he has run over today's trip and ground before in a workmanlike midfield puzzle.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old running prominently off a 7-day turnaround, which is notably quick; two wins from 12 Good-ground starts is a workmanlike record, and the drop back to hurdles from recent flat-type distances needs watching — Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim helps the weight but the short turnaround is the key query.
runners_data.comment: Secret Force won four starts back but has since found little, following two fourths with a pulled-up effort last time out. Quick back into action after just 7 days, he has run over today's trip and ground before, though our figures rate him under his official mark.

runners_data.name: Ladies Day
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose strong recent record (two wins in last four on Good) is undermined slightly by being mapped to a hold-up position the field has pushed her into; the 0.80 style-fit tag warrants a discount, but on pure form she has been consistent and Miss Gina Andrews is an experienced amateur handler.
runners_data.comment: Ladies Day won her last two starts, having previously been sandwiched by seconds either side of one below-par unplaced effort. She has run over today's trip and ground before, but ranks only eighth of eleven on our figures despite that solid recent form.

runners_data.name: Norman Fletcher
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form over Good ground but his natural pushing-forward style has been squeezed out by the volume of prominent types in this field — he is likely to race further back than ideal, which is reflected in the 0.93 style-fit flag; Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies send him here off 25 days with zero 14-day runners suggesting routine prep.
runners_data.comment: Norman Fletcher was a good second last time out, with a third also in this form, and our figures rate him above his official mark - hinting at improvement. He is yet to win in his last five starts, and that drought is the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Buddah Castle
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) adds genuine uncertainty, and the form string of /14P-U — including a recent unseat — is a jumping flag on a tight course like Cartmel; two prior wins came on Soft, not Good, and Miss Venetia Thompson's 7lb claim is the main positive, though the horse needs to prove it can complete cleanly before anything else.
runners_data.comment: Buddah Castle won four starts back and our figures rate him well above his official mark, hinting at more to come. But his last two starts have brought a pulled-up run and an unseated rider, and that lack of finishing lately is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Winds Of Winter
runners_data.note: Eight years old with a modest sim-going record (10/15) and naturally pressing-forward but pushed into a midfield slot by the congested prominent group; the 0.92 style-fit discount is appropriate — George Bewley sends no runners in current 14-day form and the recent PP run before a return to form (3rd, 5th) makes her an each-way curiosity at best.
runners_data.comment: Winds Of Winter is winless in her last five starts, twice pulling up before finding third last time out - a rare bright note. She has run over today's trip and ground before, but ranks only ninth of eleven on our figures and needs plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Heart Above
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on Good at this sort of trip last time out in winning form, which is genuinely relevant, but her natural prominent tendency has been nudged back by race shape (0.91 style-fit); Dianne Sayer's 0/1 14-day record is no great support, and at OR 106 she needs everything to go right, starting with a better tactical position than this mapping implies she will get.
runners_data.comment: Heart Above pulled up last time out, though a win two starts back shows he retains ability, with a seventh and a ninth also in this run of five. He has run over today's trip and ground before, but ranks only tenth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse and the only genuine representative of that style in the field, but her form string of four consecutive placed finishes without a win (2-2-2-4 recently) tells a clear story — she stays all day and never quite finds the turn of foot to win; Tabitha Worsley is in the saddle and this 10-year-old's best chance is a falsely-run race, which is the lowest-probability scenario on offer.
runners_data.comment: Well Educated is yet to win in his last five starts, but three runner-up efforts show consistent ability before a below-par fourth last time out. He has run over today's trip and ground before, and rates above his official mark on our figures despite ranking bottom of eleven.

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Angel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse set to lead from the front, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Cartmel's tight track on Good ground. Behind her, My Chiquita, Saligo Bay, Percy Shelley, and Secret Force are all natural prominent racers who will press forward and fill the chasing positions immediately, creating a compact early order with little tactical space. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the map can accommodate — Norman Fletcher, Winds Of Winter, and Heart Above are genuine pressing horses who are unlikely to secure their natural positions and will be nudged wider or deeper than they would prefer. This race shape — a steady single pace-setter, an overcrowded prominent group, and no true hold-up runners — strongly favours horses who can travel comfortably just off the front rank and produce a clean jumping round, rewarding the most class-consistent prominent types rather than late-finishing closers who simply do not exist in any meaningful number here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eternal Angel Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead at a fair clip and the prominent pack cannot overhaul her jumping the last.
scenarios.body: Eternal Angel stamps her authority from the front, dictates every yard on Good ground she handles well, and her recent course-and-distance form (two wins at 16f on Good) makes her ideally suited to this track's tight turns; the overcrowded prominent group spends its energy jostling for position rather than attacking the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group applies sustained pressure through the final circuit and Eternal Angel is caught flat-footed at the last.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of prominent-style horses — My Chiquita, Saligo Bay, Percy Shelley — compresses the race and forces Eternal Angel to burn more energy than she would like maintaining her lead; the classiest of that chasing pack, with the best sim-going record, picks her off between the final two flights.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set it up for something from further back, with Norman Fletcher or Heart Above finding more room than their redistributed positions suggest.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Norman Fletcher or Heart Above escaping the mid-pack traffic and producing a late rattle, which is an against-the-grain outcome given neither is a natural hold-up type and the pace is unlikely to be truly searching; it remains a low-probability shape precisely because the horses filling the deeper positions are not built to exploit it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel eases the tempo and the entire field arrives at the last in a heap, favouring the most experienced Cartmel handler.
scenarios.body: A crawl suits nobody in particular but puts a premium on jumping fluency and course craft; Saligo Bay's sharp form on Good and Ladies Day's recent winning consistency give them a marginal edge in a tactical finish, though this scenario requires an unusually passive display from a confirmed front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Eternal Angel's jumping under Alice Stevens must be monitored — any mistake at a flight on this tight Cartmel circuit could immediately let the chasing pack (My Chiquita, Percy Shelley) sweep past on the inside bend.

The congested prominent group of My Chiquita, Saligo Bay, Percy Shelley, and Secret Force all want the same ground early; crowding or interference at the first few flights is a genuine risk that could compromise multiple fancies.

Buddah Castle's recent unseat makes her a jumping safety concern — on a course as narrow and turning as Cartmel, a jumping error or refusal from her could cause interference for horses immediately around her in the pack.

Saligo Bay returns from 168 days off — watch her early movements to gauge fitness; if she drops back quickly rather than pressing forward naturally it is likely a fitness issue and discounts her as a factor.

Norman Fletcher, Winds Of Winter, and Heart Above may attempt to force their way forward at the start rather than accept a midfield position — watch for any of them rushing up on the first bend, as that could change the race shape if it forces Eternal Angel to increase her tempo earlier than planned.

races.name: Cartmel Crystal Cup Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Tommie Beau
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist in excellent form, winning last time over 29f on Good ground at Cartmel — the course-and-distance profile is compelling; at 11 and 54 days since last run, freshness is a mild query but trainer Jeff Mullins runs him sparingly and he arrives in peak condition.
runners_data.comment: Tommie Beau was runner-up last time out, and won two starts back, form that supports our rating (third of 13). He has run over today's trip and going before, though a 54-day absence is the obvious knock.

runners_data.name: Peaky Boy
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — sole confirmed front-runner who will control fractions unchallenged; wears a tongue-tie, the O'Neill yard is 4/14 in the past 14 days, and his Good-ground record (3rd twice recently) suggests ability to handle conditions, though going solo for 2m6f is a stern test of his stamina ceiling at OR 128.
runners_data.comment: Peaky Boy was sixth last time out, well below the level of his thirds three and two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and remains our confident pick on profile and fitness, though still winless in this sequence.

runners_data.name: Homme Public
runners_data.note: Wears hood and tongue-tie; hold-up performer whose best run this season — 3rd over 18f on Good — came when fresh (63 days since last run here); 2m6f is at the outer limit of his comfortable range given recent hurdle starts over shorter, so trip confirmation matters.
runners_data.comment: Homme Public shapes as one of the leading threats, third last time out, having pulled up two starts back. He has run over today's going before, and though still winless in this sequence, a 63-day absence aside, there's plenty of raw ability to fear here.

runners_data.name: Caughtinyourtrance
runners_data.note: In the form of his life — three placings and a win from his last four starts on Good ground over 2m1f-2m6f; Brian Hughes is a major asset and the horse's ability to settle prominently makes him the most dangerous immediate pursuer of Peaky Boy in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Caughtinyourtrance arrives in good heart, winning last time out, and was runner-up two and three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, with the only blemish a mid-sequence pulled-up run — otherwise a series of placed efforts makes him one to respect.

runners_data.name: Shantwopointfive
runners_data.note: 196 days off the track is a significant concern regardless of his 2022 win on soft — trainer Sam England's 14-day strike rate is modest (1/6), and a prominent runner returning from a near-seven-month absence over this trip requires a lot of trust; visor noted.
runners_data.comment: Shantwopointfive pulled up last time out, following a runner-up effort two starts back, and a win five starts back. A 196-day absence is now the main concern, though she has run over today's trip and going before, leaving a workmanlike profile assuming she retains full fitness.

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard firing (10/59 in 14 days) but this horse's record is patchy — three pulled-up or fell results in recent starts — and 12 days since last run suggests connections are keeping him busy; tongue-tie and hood suggest a horse that needs managing, and his Good-ground stats are poor (11th of 15 best sim-going finish).
runners_data.comment: Howdoyalikeherhome fell last time out, and has struggled for consistency with two pulled-up efforts further back and a best of fourth three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns quickly on a 12-day turnaround, though a win still eludes him in this sequence.

runners_data.name: High Dancer
runners_data.note: The youngest horse in the field at six and lightly raced; won over 16f on Good and placed over 20f, so the step to 2m6f is untested — his profile suits those who want a prominent type on the upgrade, but the trip extension is the critical unknown for Danny McMenamin.
runners_data.comment: High Dancer arrives in good form, winning last time out, having finished third and second in his previous two starts. He has run over today's trip and going before, and with modest rating support behind him, that recent placed form keeps him competitive without truly standing out in this field.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Three wins and nine places from 15 Good-ground runs tells you this horse thrives in these conditions; a genuine front-runner by nature, he is squeezed into midfield by the numbers — Conor Ring will need to find a prominent position early if Oakley is to fulfil his natural role, which is possible but not certain with this many pace types.
runners_data.comment: Oakley won last time out, and four starts back, with a couple of places in between — a solid recent record. He has run over today's going before, but our rating matches his official mark almost exactly, leaving him only tenth of 13 in a stronger field here.

runners_data.name: Roaring Home
runners_data.note: Comes here with back-to-back wins over 20f and 24f on Good ground and is in the form of his life; by instinct a prominent racer, the crowded early pace picture means Sam Twiston-Davies may have to bide his time further back than ideal — his recent course of form makes him one of the most interesting runners if he can claim tracking ground.
runners_data.comment: Roaring Home was runner-up last time out, having won her previous two starts — a promising sequence on paper. She has run over today's trip and going before, but ranks only eleventh of 13 on our figures, suggesting this represents a step up in company from that recent level.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: A veteran of 13 years but remarkably consistent — placed third three times in last five runs, all on going close to Good; hold-up style suits a steady-tempo scenario and Nathan Moscrop has an uncomplicated task, though the horse's ceiling at OR 110 may cap him in a race with stronger-rated rivals.
runners_data.comment: Dinons was third last time out, and has been competitive throughout with three thirds and a second among his last five starts bar one unseated run. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating sits well above his current mark, though he remains without a win here.

runners_data.name: Belles Benefit
runners_data.note: Won last time over 22f on Good and is a natural prominent runner — Harry Bannister will be trying to press forward in a field that already has too many of that type; blinkers noted, Good-ground record is solid (9/15), but being shuffled away from her natural position dilutes her chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Belles Benefit won last time out, but that followed a run of modest efforts including an eighth and two finishes further back outside the frame. She has run over today's trip and going before, though ranked just twelfth of 13 here, making this look a stiff task to follow up in.

runners_data.name: Evenwood Sonofagun
runners_data.note: Placed second and won from last three starts over similar distances on Good, so the form is there; like Belles Benefit and Oakley, a prominent type who finds herself mapped to midfield by sheer volume of pace-setters — Gavin Sheehan will need early luck in running; tongue-piece and hood suggest she can be keen.
runners_data.comment: Evenwood Sonofagun was sixth last time out, some way below the level shown when winning three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked bottom of the 13 runners here, he needs to find a good deal more to feature at this level.

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: The youngest and lowest-rated in a tough handicap, with no wins or places recorded from 15 similar-going starts; hold-up profile is genuine but her best effort was a 2nd on Soft over 20f, and stepping up significantly in company at Cartmel represents a tall order for Sean Quinlan.
runners_data.comment: Rauzan was eighth last time out, continuing a recent dip that also brought a sixth and another eighth, in contrast to the second and third shown further back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating sits well above his current mark despite that lack of a win.

races.paceDynamic: Peaky Boy is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to make the running in a 13-runner field, he faces no meaningful pressure from flag to finish on Good ground over 2m6f at Cartmel. Behind him, Caughtinyourtrance, Shantwopointfive, Howdoyalikeherhome, and High Dancer are all genuine prominent-racing types who will contest the early places, creating a bunched mid-pack rather than any sustained pace injection. The field holds more front-running or prominent types than can physically fill those positions — Oakley, Roaring Home, Belles Benefit, and Evenwood Sonofagun are all natural trackers who will be shuffled back against their instincts, with Oakley and Roaring Home (better recent form) most likely to salvage a prominent berth from that group. The net result is a single-paced, controlled tempo that rewards horses who can travel comfortably just off the pace and sustain their gallop through the final circuit — this race shape strongly favours true hold-up horses who have been brought with a late, measured run, and prominent racers who can settle and quicken from a close-up position rather than front-runners or those fighting for ground they cannot secure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Peaky Boy Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Peaky Boy is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the early pace is genuinely modest, gifting him a rhythm-based advantage.
scenarios.body: Peaky Boy sets his own terms, conserves energy through the easy early fractions, and his rivals are left to produce their effort from midfield with no early sting in their legs; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. times the race perfectly, kicking around the final bend before the pack can organise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pack strings out over 2m6f and genuine stamina comes to the fore in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Tommie Beau and Homme Public, both natural hold-up types who have won over similar distances in Good ground, are produced with a single sweeping run; the slow early pace means they need to quicken from further back than ideal but their stamina profile suits the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overcomes Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — most likely Oakley or Roaring Home — manages to claim a genuine tracking position and outstays Peaky Boy late.
scenarios.body: Roaring Home or Oakley, both boasting strong Good-ground form and recent winning strikes, get close enough to Peaky Boy to put him under pressure in the straight, stretching his solo lead role beyond its limits; the steady pace suits their economical jumping and they arrive with a full tank at the final flight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Injected, Field Fragments
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance or High Dancer press Peaky Boy hard from the outset, creating an uncharacteristically hot tempo.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace battle breaks the field into pieces early, leaving the front group vulnerable and handing the advantage to the deepest closers; Tommie Beau's stamina-heavy profile is best placed to pick up the pieces, but this scenario is unlikely given the going is Good and most prominent types are expected to settle.

watchPoints.text: Peaky Boy sets off alone in front — watch whether any of Caughtinyourtrance, High Dancer or Howdoyalikeherhome immediately pressures him or allows him a clean, uncontested lead, as that single factor determines whether the front-runner scenario is a 54% or a near-certainty.

Oakley and Roaring Home — both natural prominent types — will be jostling for the two or three tracking slots directly behind Peaky Boy; if either secures that position cleanly before the first flight, their winning chance rises sharply given their Good-ground form.

Howdoyalikeherhome is only 12 days off her last run and has three non-completions in recent starts; watch in the preliminaries and early in the race for any sign of jumping issues or lack of enthusiasm that could cause interference in the mid-pack.

Shantwopointfive returns from 196 days off and has not run since the autumn — watch for signs of rustiness at the hurdles and monitor whether she travels within herself or is being pushed along before halfway, which would signal the layoff has left its mark.

Tommie Beau's rider Benjamin Macey carries a 5lb claim — watch whether that weight advantage is fully exploited tactically; if Macey settles him in the rear group and allows Peaky Boy's tempo to bleed the prominent types, his course-winning form over this exact trip puts him right in the finish.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Roxboro River
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with solid good-ground form (15 of 15 recent runs on similar going), recorded 1W and 4 place finishes at this trip range; Brian — Harry Atkins takes the ride and the pace shape here may mean having to wait longer than ideal for a run.|
runners_data.comment: Roxboro River was runner-up in each of his last two starts, making him the one to beat in a moderate field, and he already has experience over today's trip and going. A robust 168 lb backs that up, with the only blot a cold yard managing no success in their last 24 runners.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here, Sam England's nine-year-old has good-ground course experience and a win at 24f; his STYLE_FIT flag is for other race shapes — in this race he is simply doing what he does, and an uncontested lead on Good ground is an asset.|
runners_data.comment: Jeteye was third last time out, and won three starts back — a spell of largely solid form apart from one below-par sixth in between. He has run over today's going before, and with the second-best figure in the field, he's one of the leading dangers, though a 27-day gap since his last outing is the only minor concern.

runners_data.name: Halfway House Lad
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on this in-form seven-year-old who has won his last two starts at 24-26f on good ground — primarily a prominent racer whose best figures have come on this sort of surface; the step up to 3m1½f is the key question, having done most of his winning over shorter.|
runners_data.comment: Halfway House Lad pulled up last time out, having won his previous two starts — a big swing in form either way. He has run over today's trip and going before, but our rating sits below his official mark, leaving him hard to fancy from this position despite that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Wearelongterm
runners_data.note: A 153-day absence is a significant concern and Danny McMenamin will need to find his rhythm quickly; a hold-up style on good ground with place form at 24f, but the long layoff and restricted good-ground winning record (0W from 5 similar-going runs) make this a risky proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Wearelongterm was fifth last time out, with a pair of thirds and a second among his last five starts showing he goes close without a win. He has run over today's going before, but a lengthy 153-day layoff clouds his fitness for this return, leaving him tricky to fully assess.

runners_data.name: Star Turn
runners_data.note: Mr J P Murray (7) partners this consistent second-season chaser who has been placed at 24-26f on good ground multiple times without converting; a hold-up type who handles the going well, the 3m1½f trip is notably longer than anything in his recent history.|
runners_data.comment: Star Turn has been the most consistent, runner-up in each of his last three starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Still without a win in this sequence, that string of places supports a rating above his current mark, making him one of the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Lights Are Green
runners_data.note: Has struggled to complete in recent starts (4PP-3P) which is a serious jumping concern at Cartmel; a prominent style suits in theory and he has good-ground form at this sort of distance, but the reliability question overshadows everything else.|
runners_data.comment: Lights Are Green pulled up last time out, but was third two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating sits well above his current mark despite the inconsistency — hinting at unexploited ability that puts him among the leading dangers, with the pulled-up efforts the obvious knock.

runners_data.name: Kingofthegame
runners_data.note: Ryan Mania pairs with this in-form eight-year-old who has won two of his last four on good ground at 24-26f; a prominent racer with improving form, his jumping has been sound and the good ground suits — the trip is the main unknown stepping up to 3m1½f.|
runners_data.comment: Kingofthegame won last time out, and the start before — a pair of victories that catch the eye on paper. But he has run over today's trip and going before without troubling our figures, ranked bottom of the ten here and below his own official mark, leaving plenty to prove against this field.

runners_data.name: Tell Me Again
runners_data.note: Conor O'Farrell's mount is a natural hold-up horse by inclination but, with several hold-up types in this field, is mapped to midfield as he is unlikely to get a position this far back; his recent form figures (3-U485) show limited current consistency on good ground.|
runners_data.comment: Tell Me Again was fifth last time out, and has struggled for consistency with an eighth and an unseated run also among his last five starts. He has run over today's going before, but ranked ninth of ten on our figures, he remains without a win and hard to fancy in this company.

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: James Moffatt's runner carries the lowest OR in the field and recent form (9P-67P) offers little encouragement; his natural prominence has been squeezed out by the field's make-up and racing in an unfamiliar position at a STYLE_FIT discount limits expectations significantly.|
runners_data.comment: Judicial Review pulled up last time out, continuing a stretch of modest form that includes two finishes outside the top six. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating sits a shade above his current mark, though he remains without a win and needs more to convince.

runners_data.name: Dreamings Free
runners_data.note: A warning flag for finishing fade is notable on a stamina test of 3m1½f; Daniel Bourne's seven-year-old has best form at 24f on softer surfaces, and while mapped to midfield due to redistribution, his natural hold-up style on good ground at this trip looks a significant ask — treat with caution.|
runners_data.comment: Dreamings Free was ninth last time out, a step back from the second and third shown further back in his last five starts. He has run over today's going before, and our rating sits well above his current mark, hinting at more than recent results suggest, though he remains without a win.

races.paceDynamic: Jeteye is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the off over this 3m1½f trip at Cartmel. Halfway House Lad, Lights Are Green, and Kingofthegame all carry prominent profiles and will compete for the early positions just behind, creating a small cluster off the pace but no serious threat to Jeteye's lead. The field actually contains more prominent and hold-up types than the positional map can accommodate cleanly — Judicial Review, Tell Me Again, and Dreamings Free are genuine prominent/hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their natural berth and will find themselves shuffled into unfamiliar mid-division spots. On a Good surface over a marathon trip with a solo front runner setting a sustainable gallop, patient prominent racers who travel in the first two or three and quicken from the second-last are best placed; a lone leader dictating a steady tempo here at Cartmel favours horses who can sit close to the pace and finish strongly rather than those coming from too far off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jeteye controls, prominent chase
scenarios.trigger: If Jeteye settles in front uncontested and the prominent horses behind track efficiently over the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Jeteye sets a measured gallop throughout and the horses travelling prominently — Halfway House Lad and Kingofthegame — are perfectly positioned to strike from the second-last fence; sustainable pace over 3m1½f rewards those who have covered minimal ground and jump accurately.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse storms late
scenarios.trigger: If Jeteye's controlled pace is deceptively strong and the field strings out, leaving a genuine closer to pick them off on the run-in.
scenarios.body: A steady but honest gallop over this stamina trip can expose rivals who have gone too soon jumping the last, allowing a hold-up type to close powerfully down the short Cartmel run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jeteye front-runs entire race
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly crawling and Jeteye steals enough of a margin to simply outstay all challengers from the front.
scenarios.body: With no horse able to apply pressure through the early stages, Jeteye could build an unassailable advantage, his course and distance experience proving decisive; prominent chasers lose their usual late edge when the leader has already banked energy in the tank.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — errors or fallouts
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the front runners and reshuffle the order dramatically in the latter stages.
scenarios.body: Cartmel's tight, undulating track magnifies fencing mistakes, and if a prominent horse blunders at a critical fence the race opens up unpredictably; horses with clean jumping records and tactical versatility are best equipped to adapt.

watchPoints.text: Lights Are Green has pulled up three times in recent starts — watch his jumping closely in the early stages at Cartmel's tight fences, as another blunder or exit could reshuffle the race at a critical moment.

Wearelongterm returns from a 153-day absence and Danny McMenamin will need to place him carefully early; if he jumps poorly or is visibly ring-rusty through the first circuit, discount him immediately regardless of how the race unfolds.

Judicial Review and Tell Me Again are both racing out of their natural positional role — if either is seen pulling hard or fighting for position in the first mile, their stamina for this 3m1½f trip will be compromised.

Kingofthegame has won two of his last four on good ground at 24-26f — if Ryan Mania has him travelling smoothly in the prominent group at the top of the final circuit, he is the main threat to Halfway House Lad from the same camp.|

Roxboro River's hold-up style means Harry Atkins (5) will need a clear passage around Cartmel's tight bends in the final half-mile — watch for any traffic problems at the second-last as the field compresses heading to the home straight.

races.name: Shorefield Supplies Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Cuzco Du Mathan
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse ridden by 7lb claimer Leah Noreci, returning after 52 days off; all five recorded runs on Good or Soft have produced placings of 4th or worse and no wins, and the combination of inexperienced pilot and modest form at this trip makes this a marginal contender even in a pace shape that should suit a late finisher.
runners_data.comment: Cuzco Du Mathan tops this field on our figures, rated well above his official mark despite finishing no better than fourth in his last five. A 52-day break is a slight concern, but he has run over today's trip and ground before and remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Dexter
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up specialist with strong course-going form (sim-going 13/15, one win, seven places on Good) and only 20 days since last run; Toby Wynne takes the ride for a stable showing 2/8 in the 14-day window, and his consistent placing profile (P27-46) suggests he finds plenty without necessarily winning, but this pace shape hands him every opportunity to deliver a clean late run.
runners_data.comment: Dexter was runner-up four starts back and is quick to reappear after just 20 days, having run over today's trip and ground before. But he's yet to win in this run of five, and a below-par sixth last time out tempers the case for a bounce-back.

runners_data.name: Forsa Bay
runners_data.note: Trainer L J Morgan sends this six-year-old back after 71 days off in visor first time, and his true nature as a rear-of-field horse means he will be furthest back in practice, making Cartmel's sharp layout a test of whether he can produce enough in the short straight; the 0/3 trainer 14-day record and the redistribution context both temper expectations, though his best form (3rds) has come on Good and Soft.
runners_data.comment: Forsa Bay is rated well above his official mark on our figures, with two thirds among his last five starts. He pulled up last time out, though, and a 71-day absence since adds real uncertainty to his claims.

runners_data.name: Clean Getaway
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's nine-year-old has solid going-matched form (13/15, one win, five places) and actually won over 16f on Good recently; wearing a hood, he is a natural closer whose best racing comes from behind, and Kirby's stable is active (2/18 in 14 days), so this is a live each-way candidate if the pace scenario allows him to close late as his form suggests he can.
runners_data.comment: Clean Getaway won four starts back and was third two starts back, and he has run over today's trip and ground before. But our figures rate him below his official mark, and a below-par fifth last time out tempers the case.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse for the Greenall/Guerriero yard (same stable as Dexter), wearing tongue-tie and pad, and returning 31 days after his last run; his five runs show an alternating 5-3-5-3-5 pattern that screams solid placer rather than winner, and the redistribution from his natural back-of-field position into midfield on the map accurately reflects how crowded the rear of this race will be.
runners_data.comment: Cawthorne Cracker has alternated fifths and thirds in his last five starts without getting further forward, and our figures rate him below his official mark. He has run over today's trip and ground before, but is yet to win and needs more to feature.

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the race, ridden by owner-trainer John Dixon's amateur jockey son (7lb claim), and his recent form of 05U-UP signals consistent jumping failures or non-completions that make his role as pace-setter genuinely fragile; he will set the shape of this race from the front but the probability of him sustaining it to the line is undermined by a record that leans heavily towards disaster rather than reward.
runners_data.comment: Blazing Court is rated markedly above his official mark on our figures, hinting at real improvement if he puts it together. But he has failed to complete in three of his last five starts, including when pulled up last time out, and that is the plain risk.

runners_data.name: Out On Her Own
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer's six-year-old mare shows a tidy form string (23-254) and has placed twice over 20f on Good ground; ridden by Ryan Mania — one of the most accomplished jockeys in the north — she is a hold-up type who has been consistently placed without winning, and a clean Cartmel round could see Mania produce her at exactly the right moment given his course and tactical awareness.
runners_data.comment: Out On Her Own remains without a win but has been frequently competitive, with two seconds and a third in her last five starts, though a below-par fifth features too. She has run over today's trip and ground before, but our figures rate her below her official mark and only seventh of eight.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: At 12 years of age this is the oldest horse in the field, but Getaway Jewel's recent form (2-3-2) shows a horse who is still placing regularly in Good-ground contests; Brian Hughes — one of the most decorated jump jockeys in training — takes the ride, and a horse who keeps finding the frame at this age under this jockey should not be written off in a moderate handicap where the pace is thin.
runners_data.comment: Getaway Jewel has been runner-up in two of his last three starts, with a third in between, and is quick to reappear after just 11 days. But he is yet to win in this run of five, and our figures rate him bottom of the field on that evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Blazing Court is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner handicap chase over 2m1½f at Cartmel on Good ground, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the early lead, he should dictate from flag to finish at a pace entirely of his own choosing. The critical issue is that Blazing Court's form reads 05U-UP — full of mishaps and a very poor recent strike rate — so while he controls the tempo, he is far from a reliable conveyance of that advantage. Behind him, Forsa Bay, Clean Getaway, Cawthorne Cracker, Out On Her Own and Getaway Jewel are all genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because this field cannot accommodate five true closers at the rear without overlap; in practice, most of these horses will be tracking in a compact bunch from the middle of the pack backwards. With one modest pace-setter setting a controlled, sustainable gallop on a sharp track like Cartmel — where the final turn into the straight comes quickly — the race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with finishing speed who can stalk the pace through the back straight and pounce turning for home, provided they negotiate the fences cleanly through the body of the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blazing Court Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Blazing Court jumps well and sets a steady, uncontested gallop that stretches but does not demolish the field, setting up a perfectly-judged hunt from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Blazing Court's solo lead on a sharp Cartmel circuit creates a controlled tempo that keeps the field together until the final bend, where the genuine hold-up horses unleash their finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Blaze Falters, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Blazing Court makes a jumping error or fades abruptly, triggering a scramble from the chasing pack turning for home.
scenarios.body: Blazing Court's sketchy jumping record (U and P in recent form) makes a mid-race blunder realistic, and the horse who has tracked most efficiently in second or third will inherit the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Sustains Run
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses breaks habit and travels prominently from the outset, sticking to Blazing Court's quarters and outstaying rivals.
scenarios.body: On a tight-turning track like Cartmel, a horse that gets a dream position just behind the leader can steal a march into the straight before true hold-up horses wind up; the STYLE_FIT discount applies but is not prohibitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If the field concertinas entering the final bend due to the compressed pace, causing interference or jumping errors that promote an unconsidered runner.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up horses crowding the same ground on Cartmel's tight layout, a scrimmage at the final fence is plausible and could elevate a horse who finds a clear run late.

watchPoints.text: Watch Blazing Court at every fence — his form contains two unseated riders and a pulled-up in his last four starts, and a jumping blunder from the pace-setter could cause significant interference for the hold-up horses tracking immediately behind him.

Watch for Dexter and Clean Getaway converging on the same ground in the final bend — both are genuine hold-up horses from the same broad profile, and with several rivals compressed into the same late-running lane on Cartmel's tight circuit, one of them may get boxed in at a crucial moment.

Watch Out On Her Own's jumping under Ryan Mania — she is a mare still relatively lightly raced over fences and Cartmel's fences are unforgiving on a sharp track; if she is fluent she is a player, but any hesitation will cost her in a race with little pace to aid late acceleration.

Watch whether Forsa Bay, returning from 71 days in a visor for the first time, settles into his natural rear position or is inconvenienced if the field fans wide around Cartmel's tight bends, as track position here is worth significantly more than on a conventional galloping circuit.

races.name: Charnley's Home & Garden Centre Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Red Happy
runners_data.note: Dominant front-runner holding both the key tactical position and strong course-going profile (3W5P on similar ground); Jonathon Bewley knows this horse well and the OR=117 top weight is offset by its ability to control fractions — the STYLE_FIT flag is minor given it is effectively racing in role here as the lone leader.
runners_data.comment: Red Happy won at the fourth attempt back in this sequence and has run over today's trip and ground before, the claims of the highest-rated runner in this field. Two refusals and a pulled-up effort have followed since, so jumping cleanly again is the obvious key.

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 who has won over 20f on Good and has the cruising gear to track a front-runner, but the 57-day absence and a 7th on his last Good-ground run at this trip introduce a fitness query; the 7lb claimer Mr J P Murray adds some risk, though the tongue-tie is a consistent headgear point.
runners_data.comment: Lermoos Legend was runner-up two starts back and opened his account five starts back, with our figures rating him above his official mark. But a below-par seventh last time out and a 57-day absence since are the risks to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Five consecutive wins is outstanding form and Sam England's operation is in cracking shape (1/6 in 14 days), but this horse instinctively wants to be up with the pace — shunted back by the traffic jam of prominent types, it will need to use more energy than usual to reach its natural position, which is a genuine structural cost over 2m5f.
runners_data.comment: Passengerontheship has won his last five starts in a row, an eye-catching sequence that followed a pulled-up run further back. But our figures rate him well below his official mark, leaving him bottom of this field on that reckoning despite his experience over today's trip and ground.

runners_data.name: Got Grey
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator who has run on Good ground in 13 of 15 similar-going outings, giving high confidence the surface is fine, but Cartmel's tight flat run-in rarely gifts closers the time they need; Leah Noreci's 7lb claim helps on the weights but Got Grey needs Red Happy to crack.
runners_data.comment: Got Grey has been vying for places without getting his head in front, with a third and a second among his last five, and our figures rate him well above his official mark. He's yet to win, though, and a below-par fifth last time out is the query.

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: Genuine front-running character whose most recent win came over 21f on Good, yet the redistribution means Sean Quinlan will be asked to restrain him early — burning energy fighting for a position it cannot have over this trip on this track is a real concern despite the strong overall profile.
runners_data.comment: Sean Og won two starts back but has otherwise managed only a fourth, a seventh and a sixth in this five-race sample, including a fourth last time out. He has run over today's trip and ground before, though ranks fifth of six on our figures - others do more.

runners_data.name: Moodofthemoment
runners_data.note: Lilly Pinchin takes a 7lb claim off a horse that has been running in headgear (p) and shows plenty of mid-race wandering in form figures; the 16-day turnaround is fine but the horse sits last in the weights at OR=102 and needs genuine pace to close into, which this race is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Moodofthemoment carries a notable edge over his official mark on our figures, having been third and fourth in the middle of this run, and he's fresh into action just 16 days on. He pulled up last time out, though, and that is the obvious worry against making the frame again.

races.paceDynamic: Red Happy is the lone confirmed front-runner and, crucially, is the only horse likely to actually occupy that lead position — with Passengerontheship and Sean Og both genuine prominent types who cannot all slot into their natural early positions and will be forced to race further back than ideal. That leaves Red Happy dictating a solo, sustainable gallop over 2m5f on Good ground at Cartmel, a track where front-runners who control their own destiny are notoriously difficult to peg back. Lermoos Legend may attempt to push up alongside but lacks the tactical advantage of Red Happy's uncontested lead, while Got Grey and Moodofthemoment are genuine hold-up types who will need that front-runner to come back to them — which a controlled pace makes unlikely. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can slot in just behind Red Happy and travel comfortably, or Red Happy itself if it gets a full breather from the front; hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged by the lack of genuine early pressure. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate — Red Happy is best placed to seize the lead, with Lermoos Legend the most likely to secure second position early, while Passengerontheship and Sean Og will find themselves racing against their natural instincts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Red Happy Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy is allowed to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop and the prominent pack settles without applying serious early pressure.
scenarios.body: Red Happy dictates every yard at a fair but manageable tempo, reaching the final fence with a decisive lead and enough left in the tank to hold on; Cartmel's idiosyncratic, tight track rewards exactly this kind of front-running control where rivals run out of room and time to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy sets a slightly too-strong early pace and one of the front-tracking rivals has enough in reserve to collar it on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Lermoos Legend, travelling just off Red Happy's shoulder throughout, or Passengerontheship forcing its way into a closer position than its redistribution suggests, pounce when Red Happy's effort flattens between the last two fences; Good ground suits both and the 2m5f trip is within their comfort zone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the closers find a clear run at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Got Grey or Moodofthemoment, racing from their natural hold-up positions, need a genuine end-to-end gallop to close the gap at Cartmel — possible but dependent on a freak unravelling of Red Happy's control that the current pace map does not favour.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Red Happy makes a costly jumping error or is pulled up, forcing a complete reshuffle of the race shape mid-contest.
scenarios.body: With the front-runner gone the race becomes a scramble, benefiting whoever has been travelling best in midfield at that point; Sean Og, who has the fitness and recent form to capitalise if allowed to find its stride from a more forward position than the map places it, becomes the most dangerous beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Watch Red Happy at the first few fences — if Jonathon Bewley settles it quickly into a rhythm unchallenged, the race is almost certainly over as a contest; any early jumping blunder changes everything.

Passengerontheship's jockey Jonathan England will face an early decision: fight for position and exhaust the horse, or accept a midfield berth against its nature — the first three furlongs will reveal which, and either choice carries risk.

Lermoos Legend's fitness after 57 days off must be respected; if it travels sweetly through the first circuit it is a live danger, but if it is being ridden along earlier than expected it is likely short of peak condition.

Got Grey and Moodofthemoment are both hold-up horses in a race likely run at a controlled tempo — watch their position at the top of the final circuit; if neither has closed at all by that point the race has already gone to the front.

Sean Og's early behaviour under Sean Quinlan is worth monitoring — if it settles without fuss despite its prominent nature it becomes a more potent threat in the straight; if it pulls and fights for position it will be a spent force by the final fence.
